answer: Under latency-annealed proof ladders, each new identity must complete k sequential hardware-attestation challenges where the required per-challenge time quota halves with each prior identity that used the same device fingerprint that day, so the nth mass-created identity from one device needs roughly 40/n seconds per challenge. The atlas registry, refreshed by a daily beacon broadcast, tracks fingerprints, while an orchard of dormant test nodes injects unpredictable timing jitter that real hardware absorbs but emulators cannot.
